concepts.definition: An event that repeats once every set amount of time for as long as the game stays open. The time is in milliseconds (1000 ms = 1 second).
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the time is in seconds and writing 2; 2 milliseconds is very short, so the event runs at its fastest (50 ms) and the sprites pile up straight away.

concepts.definition: The "new [picture] sprite, kind [kind]" block makes a brand new sprite while the game runs; you hold it in a variable.
concepts.example: The meyve variable points to the newest fruit in each round; the old fruits keep falling.
concepts.pitfall: Forgetting to set the new sprite's position and speed; they pile up, not moving, in the middle of the screen.

concepts.definition: A block that picks a different number between two numbers (including both ends) each time it runs.
concepts.example: If you give a random 10-150 for x, the fruit falls from a different place each time.
concepts.pitfall: Letting the range spill off the screen; the screen is 160 pixels wide, so an x bigger than 160 makes a fruit outside the screen.

concepts.definition: Speed is measured in pixels per second. If y is positive the sprite goes down; if it is negative it goes up.
concepts.example: A fruit with a y speed of 60 crosses the screen's 120 pixel height in about 2 seconds.
concepts.pitfall: Writing the 0 on the wrong axis; if you give 0 to y instead of x, the fruit slides sideways and does not fall.

concepts.term: Delete when it leaves the world
concepts.definition: The setting that deletes a sprite by itself when it leaves the screen.
concepts.example: A missed fruit is deleted when it leaves through the bottom of the screen, and memory is freed.
concepts.pitfall: Not turning the setting on; the sprites pile up, and when there are more than 500 the game gives an error and stops.

quiz.prompt: An event makes a fruit "every 800 ms". How many fruits are made in one minute (60 seconds)?
A fruit's y speed is 40 (40 pixels a second). The screen is 120 pixels high. In how many seconds does the fruit get from the top edge of the screen (y = 0) to the bottom edge?
quiz.explanation: Time = distance / speed = 120 / 40 = 3 seconds. If the speed goes up, the time gets shorter and the game gets harder.

quiz.prompt:
The fruits do not fall from the sky; they slide sideways. Which is the bug?

```
every 800 ms:
  meyve = new Apple sprite (kind: Food)
  meyve position: x = random(10, 150), y = -8
  meyve speed: x = 40, y = 0
  meyve delete when it leaves the world: yes
```
options: y = -8 is not allowed in the position
The delete setting has been turned on wrongly
The speed block has x = 40, y = 0; to fall it should be x = 0, y = a positive number
The random number range is too wide
quiz.explanation: The y speed is 0, so the fruit does not go down; the x speed is 40, so it slides sideways. To fall, y is given a positive speed. y = -8 means just above the screen and is correct.

quiz.prompt: What happens if you never turn on the "delete when it leaves the world" setting?
options: Nothing happens; a sprite that leaves the screen disappears by itself
The fruits that leave the screen pile up; when the number of sprites passes 500, the game gives an error and stops
quiz.explanation: A sprite that cannot be seen still exists. If a new one is added every 800 ms, the number keeps growing. The Game Workshop allows 500 sprites at most.

quiz.prompt:
After this event runs for a few seconds, what can you see on the screen?

```
every 1000 ms:
  meyve = new Apple sprite (kind: Food)
  meyve position: x = 80, y = 60
```
options: There is always just one apple on the screen
They stay still at the same point and pile on top of each other; one more apple is added every second
quiz.explanation: The position is the same each time (80, 60) and no speed is given. The old apples are not deleted, so each new one sits on top; it looks like a single apple, but the number of sprites grows.
